issues.body: The new decision record says every added crates/<x>/Cargo.toml must also edit root Cargo.toml, citing G1 and assert_workspace_tree, and concludes that two new-crate PRs always co-hold area:workspace. That does not follow from the implementation: gate-new-crate.py's G1 requires README plus benchmark/SKILL as applicable, but never workspace membership, while assert_workspace_tree only rejects declared members missing from disk (and glob-empty trees), not an extra crate directory absent from [workspace].members. Thus a PR can add a crate manifest without touching root Cargo.toml and the claimed workspace serialization is not guaranteed. The added compute_ready fixture supplies area:workspace by construction, so it is vacuous with respect to this missing derivation/enforcement step.
issues.fix_hint: Either add an enforced gate requiring every newly added crates/<x>/Cargo.toml to be registered in root [workspace].members (and add a real test proving the changed-file/label path gives both new-crate PRs area:workspace), or revise the decision and partition behavior so correctness does not depend on that assumption. Also correct the statement that assert_workspace_tree refuses all manifest/directory disagreement, since it currently checks only the declared-but-missing direction.
issues.title: New-crate serialization premise is not enforced by the cited guards

verdict.summary: The added tests accurately pin the current segment-wise conflict behavior, but the rationale used to decline per-new-crate partitioning relies on a guarantee that the cited guards do not enforce. The self-tests pass, yet they test an assumed workspace holder rather than proving that actual new-crate PRs necessarily acquire it.
